Let
\[
A_n=\int_{[0,1]^4}e^{-n(P^2+Q^2)}\,d\mathbf x,\qquad B_n=I_n(0).
\]
Then
\[
I_n(\lambda)=A_n\sinh\lambda+B_n,
\]
so the unique root is
\[
\lambda_n=\operatorname{arsinh}\!\left(-\frac{B_n}{A_n}\right).
\]

First,
\[
A_n=J_n^2,\qquad J_n=\int_0^1 e^{-np^2}(-\log p)\,dp,
\]
because the product \(p=x_1x_2\) has density \(-\log p\) on \([0,1]\). With \(y=\sqrt n\,p\),
\[
J_n=\frac1{\sqrt n}\int_0^{\sqrt n}e^{-y^2}\left(\frac12\log n-\log y\right)\,dy
\sim \frac{\sqrt\pi}{4}\frac{\log n}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Hence
\[
A_n\sim \frac{\pi}{16}\frac{(\log n)^2}{n}.
\]

Now consider the oscillatory part \(B_n\). After the same product-variable change and then
\[
u=\delta^{-1}2^jP,\qquad v=\delta^{-1}2^kQ,
\]
the \(j,k\)-sum gives the exact leading logarithmic cancellation
\[
\sum_{j,k=0}^1(-1)^{j+k}
\bigl(-\log(\delta2^{-j}u)\bigr)
\bigl(-\log(\delta2^{-k}v)\bigr)
=(\log 2)^2.
\]
The finite upper limits may be extended to \([0,\infty)^2\), with exponentially smaller error, since the mass is concentrated near \(u,v\asymp1\). Thus
\[
B_n=\delta^2(\log2)^2\sum_{t=0}^2(-1)^t\binom2t K_t+o(\delta^6e^{-5\sqrt n}),
\]
where
\[
K_t=\int_{[0,\infty)^2}G_t(u,v)\,du\,dv.
\]

Use
\[
r=uv,\qquad s=(u-v)^2.
\]
The two branches \(u\ge v\), \(v\ge u\) have Jacobian
\[
\left|\frac{\partial(r,s)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|
=2|u-v|(u+v),
\]
while
\[
|u^2-v^2|=|u-v|(u+v),
\]
so the two branches exactly cancel the Jacobian factor. Therefore
\[
K_t=\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty C(s)
\left[1-2N(r+1)(r-a_t(s))\right]
e^{-N(4+(s-\delta)^2+(r-a_t(s))^2)}\,dr\,ds.
\]
For fixed \(s\),
\[
\left[1-2N(r+1)(r-a)\right]e^{-N(r-a)^2}
=\frac{d}{dr}\left((r+1)e^{-N(r-a)^2}\right),
\]
so
\[
K_t=-e^{-4N}\int_0^\infty C(s)e^{-N(s-\delta)^2}e^{-Na_t(s)^2}\,ds.
\]

Now put
\[
s=\delta(1+z),\qquad z\ge -1.
\]
Since \(N=\delta^{-2}\),
\[
C(s)=z-\mu,\qquad a_t(s)=1+\delta^3(z+t).
\]
Thus
\[
Na_t(s)^2=N+2\delta(z+t)+O(\delta^4(1+|z|)^2).
\]
Hence
\[
\sum_{t=0}^2(-1)^t\binom2t e^{-Na_t(s)^2}
=e^{-N}\left(4\delta^2-8\delta^3(z+1)+O(\delta^4(1+|z|)^4)\right).
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{t=0}^2(-1)^t\binom2tK_t
=-e^{-5N}\delta\int_{-1}^{\infty}(z-\mu)e^{-z^2}
\left(4\delta^2-8\delta^3(z+1)+O(\delta^4(1+|z|)^4)\right)\,dz.
\]
By the definition of \(\mu\),
\[
\int_{-1}^{\infty}(z-\mu)e^{-z^2}\,dz=0.
\]
So the first surviving term is
\[
8\delta^4e^{-5N}\int_{-1}^{\infty}z(z-\mu)e^{-z^2}\,dz
=8\mathcal M\delta^4e^{-5N}.
\]
Thus
\[
B_n\sim 8\mathcal M(\log2)^2\delta^6e^{-5N}
=8\mathcal M(\log2)^2n^{-3/2}e^{-5\sqrt n}.
\]

Since \(B_n/A_n\to0\),
\[
\lambda_n\sim-\frac{B_n}{A_n}
\sim -\frac{128\mathcal M(\log2)^2}{\pi}\,
\frac{e^{-5\sqrt n}}{\sqrt n(\log n)^2}.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{\alpha=\frac12,\qquad \beta=2,\qquad c=5,\qquad
L=-\frac{128(\log2)^2}{\pi}\mathcal M.}
\]
